issue.title: Stabilize parallel metadata-search commit-repeat test
issue.description: Proposed by sase-da.4: tests/ace/tui/test_agent_metadata_search.py::test_inline_metadata_search_commit_repeat_q_and_passthrough failed during a parallel just test run but passes in isolation (independently reconfirmed by the sase-da land audit). Investigate shared TUI/task state or timing leakage under pytest-xdist, make the test deterministic without weakening its commit-repeat and passthrough assertions, and verify it repeatedly in parallel.

evidence.note: Independent reproduction on 2026-08-03 during sase-en landing: after the dependency-floor and visual-helper fixes, full just check failed tests/ace/tui/test_agent_metadata_search.py::test_inline_metadata_search_reverse_key_override under xdist/full-suite load after 25,815 passed / 7 skipped, while the exact node passed immediately in isolation with -n 0 (1.92s call, 2.65s total). This appears to be the same metadata-search suite-load timing family as the original commit-repeat report, not a regression from the sase-core-rs floor.

payload.close_reason: Backlog triage 2026-08-05: consolidating the full-parallel-suite / xdist flake class onto umbrella task sase-ct ('Flaky ACE TUI tests under full parallel just test run'). Every one of these reports the same shape — a single node fails under the full four-to-27-worker 'just test' or 'just check' run and passes immediately in isolation — so they share a root-cause class (xdist load sensitivity and shared-state leakage across workers) rather than per-test logic bugs. Per-test detail, including sase-cu's pump-free clipboard-task diagnosis, stays readable on each bead, and a +1 with fresh evidence reopens any of them if a specific node turns into a deterministic failure.
